Adjectives After Ein and Eine: German A2 Practice

Study four German examples with English meanings, then try four questions and check the explained answers.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the rule

After ein-words, adjectives use mixed endings. Where ein has no ending, the adjective supplies the gender signal: ein kleiner Hund, ein altes Haus. Feminine nominative is eine kleine Katze. Other case combinations differ: einen kleinen Hund, mit einem kleinen Hund.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not use the same ending after every form of ein: masculine nominative needs -er, while masculine accusative uses -en.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ein kleiner Hund wartet am Zaun.A small dog waits by the fence.
Worked example 2Eine nette Kollegin hilft mir.A nice colleague helps me.
Worked example 3Wir mieten ein altes Haus.We rent an old house.
Worked example 4Er spricht mit einem jungen Musiker.He speaks with a young musician.

Practice: fill in the gaps

Add the correct adjective ending after the indefinite article shown. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ein ___ Apfel liegt im Korb. (grün)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: grüner

Masculine nominative after ein needs -er on the adjective.

Question 2. Sie kauft eine ___ Lampe. (modern)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: moderne

Feminine accusative after eine takes -e.

Question 3. Ich sehe einen ___ Vogel. (bunt)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: bunten

Masculine accusative after einen takes -en.

Question 4. Wir wohnen in einem ___ Dorf. (klein)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: kleinen

Dative after einem takes -en on the adjective.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
